title: Russian Sabotage in Europe Is No Longer ‘Symbolic’
gist: Estonia's counterintelligence chief Margo Palloson says Russian sabotage in Europe has shifted from symbolic vandalism to attacks aimed at disrupting defense supplies to Ukraine, exemplified by an August attack on robotics firm Milrem. Operations increasingly use explosives, criminal proxies and layered intermediaries, while some European counterparts complain their legal tools are inadequate.

insights.claim: According to Estonia's counterintelligence chief, Russian sabotage in Estonia has moved from symbolic targets (vandalized cars, burned Ukrainian flags, arson at a Ukrainian restaurant) to attacks intended to disrupt military supplies to Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Sam Skove
insights.so_what: European defense contractors supplying Ukraine now face elevated physical-security and operational-disruption risk.
